identity: Journalist and trade unionist · United States · 1897–1980
title: Dorothy Day's birth chart
metaDescription: Dorothy Day's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 16.6° Scorpio. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Four of the ten placements whose signs are settled stand in Scorpio — the Sun, Mercury, Mars and Uranus. The placements whose signs could change with an unknown hour are not counted. A cluster that size becomes the section the rest of the chart plays around.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun's position resolves to 16.6° Scorpio — deep enough in the second decan (10°–20°) that Jupiter, its traditional sub-ruler, colours the reading.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: Closer in, Mercury stands at 16.9° Scorpio; Venus stands at 22.8° Libra; Mars stands at 20.4° Scorpio. The tradition reads thought steeped in tone and memory from Mercury, attraction that begins as conversation from Venus, effort that surges when it matters from Mars.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Start where the chart is tightest — the Sun conjunction Mercury, 0.3° of separation. The tradition stops reading a conjunction as two things. It is one appetite with two names, and it moves together or not at all. Behind it, Venus trine Neptune at 0.8°, and Jupiter sextile Saturn at 0.9° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. The unknown hour cannot unmake any of this: every aspect named survived all twenty-five samples of the day.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: The Moon makes no major aspect that survives the day; the old reading gives such a planet autonomy — it acts alone, sometimes loudly.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The oldest layer of the scheme — seven planets, four conditions — flags three placements in this chart. The Moon in Taurus at 8.9° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Venus in Libra at 22.8° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Mars in Scorpio at 20.4° is in domicile. Dignity is a statement about conditions, not about worth.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Counting only the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the chart runs 4 water, 4 air, 1 earth, 1 fire by element and 5 fixed, 3 mutable, 2 cardinal by modality. A water emphasis reads as porousness: the room is registered whole, long before it is analysed in parts. Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — the optical reversal the tradition reads as review — energy turned over before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Taurus for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 12.0° between midnight and midnight. That is quick enough to make the exact degree a neighbourhood rather than an address, and slow enough to leave the sign settled. At the noon reference it stands at 8.9°.
